metadata.title: Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps
metadata.authors: Mikhael Gromov (with an appendix by Jacques Tits)
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Word norm on a finitely generated group
nodes.statement: For a group $\Gamma$ generated by $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k$, each $\gamma\in\Gamma$ can be written as a word $\gamma_{i_1}^{p_1}\cdots\gamma_{i_t}^{p_t}$; the norm $\|\gamma\|$ is the minimal word length $\sum |p_j|$ over all such representations.
nodes.statement_clean: Norm of a group element is the minimal length of a word in the chosen generators representing it.

nodes.name: Ball $B(r)$ in a finitely generated group
nodes.statement: $B(r)\subset\Gamma$ denotes the ball of radius $r$ centered at the identity: $B(r)=\{\gamma\in\Gamma : \|\gamma\|\le r\}$. Let $\#B(r)$ be its cardinality.
nodes.statement_clean: Ball of radius r is the set of group elements with norm at most r.

nodes.name: Polynomial growth of a group
nodes.statement: A finitely generated group $\Gamma$ has polynomial growth if there exist constants $C,d>0$ such that $\#B(r)\le C r^d$ for all $r\ge 1$. The notion is independent of the chosen generating set.
nodes.statement_clean: Group has polynomial growth if its ball cardinalities grow at most polynomially.

nodes.name: Almost nilpotent (almost solvable) group
nodes.statement: A group $\Gamma$ is almost nilpotent (resp. almost solvable) if it contains a nilpotent (resp. solvable) subgroup of finite index.
nodes.statement_clean: A group is almost nilpotent if it has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.

nodes.name: Expanding map
nodes.statement: A map $f:X\to Y$ between metric spaces is globally expanding if $\mathrm{dist}(f(x_1),f(x_2))>\mathrm{dist}(x_1,x_2)$ for all $x_1\ne x_2$. It is expanding if every $x\in X$ has a neighborhood on which $f$ is globally expanding.
nodes.statement_clean: Map is expanding if locally every point has a neighborhood on which the map strictly increases distances.

nodes.name: Infra-nil-manifold and expanding infra-nil-endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a simply connected nilpotent Lie group; $\mathrm{Aff}(L)$ is generated by left translations and automorphisms. If $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{Aff}(L)$ acts freely and discretely with compact quotient $X=L/\Gamma$, then $X$ is an infra-nil-manifold; an expanding automorphism $L\to L$ respecting $\Gamma$ induces an expanding infra-nil-endomorphism $X\to X$.
nodes.statement_clean: Infra-nil-manifold is a compact quotient of a nilpotent Lie group by a discrete affine group, with an expanding induced map.

nodes.name: Topological conjugacy
nodes.statement: Maps $f:X\to X$ and $g:Y\to Y$ are topologically conjugate if there is a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two maps are topologically conjugate when they are intertwined by a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Geometric (volume) growth of a Riemannian manifold
nodes.statement: For a Riemannian manifold $Y$ and $y\in Y$, $\mathrm{Vol}_y(r)$ is the volume of the $r$-ball about $y$; the growth of $Y$ is the asymptotic behavior of $\mathrm{Vol}_y(r)$ as $r\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Geometric growth measures how the volume of metric balls grows with radius.

nodes.name: Hausdorff distance and modified Hausdorff distance
nodes.statement: For metric spaces $X,Y$, the Hausdorff distance $H(X,Y)$ is $\inf_\delta H_\delta(X,Y)$ over all admissible metrics $\delta$ on $X\sqcup Y$. For pointed spaces $(X,x),(Y,y)$, $H((X,x),(Y,y))$ is the infimum of $\varepsilon>0$ such that some admissible $\delta$ has $\delta(x,y)<\varepsilon$ and the balls $B_x(1/\varepsilon)$, $B_y(1/\varepsilon)$ are within the $\varepsilon$-neighborhoods of the other space.
nodes.statement_clean: Hausdorff distance measures how close two metric spaces (or pointed spaces) can be embedded into a common metric.

nodes.name: Pointed Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of pointed metric spaces
nodes.statement: $(X_j,x_j)\to (Y,y)$ if $\lim_j H((X_j,x_j),(Y,y))=0$. For proper $X_j$, if balls $B_{x_j}(r)$ converge in $H$ for arbitrarily large $r$, a subsequence converges to a proper pointed space.
nodes.statement_clean: Pointed metric spaces converge if their Hausdorff distance to a limit pointed space tends to zero.

nodes.name: Uniform compactness of a family of metric spaces
nodes.statement: A family $\{X_j\}$ of compact metric spaces is uniformly compact if their diameters are uniformly bounded and, for each $\varepsilon>0$, every $X_j$ can be covered by $N(\varepsilon)$ balls of radius $\varepsilon$ (equivalently every $X_j$ contains at most $M(\varepsilon)$ disjoint balls of radius $\varepsilon$).
nodes.statement_clean: Family is uniformly compact when ball-coverings are uniformly controlled across the family.

nodes.name: Rescaled metric space $\lambda X$
nodes.statement: For metric space $X$ with metric $\mathrm{dist}$, $\lambda X$ denotes $X$ equipped with the rescaled metric $\mathrm{dist}_\lambda = \lambda^{-1}\mathrm{dist}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Rescaling a metric space by lambda divides distances by lambda.

nodes.name: Regular radius for a group of polynomial growth
nodes.statement: For a group of growth $d<\infty$ and $b(r)=\#B(r)$, a number $r$ is $i$-regular if (a) $\log b(2^{-j}r)\ge \log b(r)-j(d+1)\log 2$ for $j=1,\ldots,i$, and (b) $\log b(2^j r)\le \log b(r)+\xi_j$ for $j=1,\ldots,i$, where $\xi_j=16^{j+1}(d+1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An i-regular radius satisfies upper and lower volume-doubling control compatible with polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Displacement function $D(\gamma,r)$
nodes.statement: $D(\gamma,r)=\sup_\beta \mathrm{dist}(\gamma\beta,\beta)$ where $\beta$ runs over the $r$-ball in $\Gamma$ around the identity. For a subgroup $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ generated by $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k$: $D(\Gamma',r)=\sup_{1\le j\le k} D(\gamma_j,r)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Displacement function bounds how far a group element moves the points of an r-ball.

nodes.name: f-length and polynomial f-growth (filtered group)
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be nilpotent with filtration $\Gamma=\Gamma_1\supseteq\Gamma_2\supseteq\cdots$ satisfying $[\Gamma_i,\Gamma_j]\subseteq\Gamma_{i+j}$ and $\Gamma_i=\{1\}$ for large $i$. For an $f$-generating set $E$ with $E_i=E\cap\Gamma_i$, $E_i'=E_i\setminus E_{i+1}$, the $f$-length of a word is $(n_1,n_2,\ldots)$ where $n_i$ is the count of $E_i'\cup E_i'^{-1}$ letters. $\Gamma$ has polynomial $f$-growth of degree $\le d$ if $f(r,r^2,r^3,\ldots)\le c\,r^d+1$.
nodes.statement_clean: f-length tracks generator usage by filtration level; polynomial f-growth bounds counts of elements when level i contributes r^i.

nodes.name: Main theorem (Gromov's polynomial growth theorem)
nodes.statement: If a finitely generated group $\Gamma$ has polynomial growth, then $\Gamma$ contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
nodes.statement_clean: A finitely generated group of polynomial growth is virtually nilpotent.
conclusions: $\Gamma$ is almost nilpotent (contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index)

nodes.name: Geometric corollary
nodes.statement: An expanding self-map of an arbitrary compact manifold is topologically conjugate to an infra-nil-endomorphism.
nodes.statement_clean: Expanding maps on compact manifolds are classified up to conjugacy as infra-nil-endomorphisms.
assumptions: $f:X\to X$ is an expanding self-map of a compact manifold $X$
conclusions: $f$ is topologically conjugate to an expanding infra-nil-endomorphism

nodes.name: Shub's classification of expanding maps
nodes.statement: An expanding self-map of a compact manifold $X$ is uniquely determined, up to topological conjugacy, by its action on the fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expanding maps on compact manifolds are determined up to conjugacy by their action on the fundamental group.
nodes.origin_citation: M. Shub, Expanding maps, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. XIV (1970)

nodes.name: Shub's criterion
nodes.statement: An expanding self-map of a compact manifold $X$ is topologically conjugate to an expanding infra-nil-endomorphism if and only if $\pi_1(X)$ contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
nodes.statement_clean: Conjugacy to an infra-nil-endomorphism is equivalent to virtual nilpotence of the fundamental group.
assumptions: $f:X\to X$ is an expanding self-map of a compact manifold $X$
conclusions: $f$ is topologically conjugate to an expanding infra-nil-endomorphism iff $\pi_1(X)$ is almost nilpotent

nodes.name: Polynomial growth property (Franks)
nodes.statement: If a compact manifold $X$ admits an expanding self-map then $\pi_1(X)$ has polynomial growth.
nodes.statement_clean: Existence of an expanding map forces polynomial growth on the fundamental group.
assumptions: $X$ is a compact manifold admitting an expanding self-map

nodes.name: Milnor-Wolf theorem on solvable groups
nodes.statement: A finitely generated solvable group $\Gamma$ has exponential growth unless $\Gamma$ contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
nodes.statement_clean: Solvable groups are either of exponential growth or virtually nilpotent.

nodes.name: Tits alternative for finitely generated linear groups
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a Lie group with finitely many components and $G\subset L$ be finitely generated. Either (a) $G$ contains a free group of rank 2 (and so has exponential growth), or (b) $G$ is almost solvable (and has exponential growth unless almost nilpotent).
nodes.statement_clean: Finitely generated subgroups of Lie groups are either virtually solvable or contain a free subgroup.

nodes.name: Jordan's theorem on finite subgroups of Lie groups
nodes.statement: For each Lie group $L$ with finitely many components there is a number $q$ such that every finite subgroup in $L$ contains an Abelian subgroup of index at most $q$.
nodes.statement_clean: Finite subgroups of a Lie group contain Abelian subgroups of bounded index.

nodes.name: Montgomery-Zippin theorem
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be a finite-dimensional, locally compact, connected, locally connected metric space. If the isometry group $L$ of $Y$ acts transitively on $Y$, then $L$ is a Lie group with finitely many connected components.
nodes.statement_clean: Transitive isometry group of a nice finite-dimensional metric space is a Lie group with finitely many components.
assumptions: $Y$ is finite-dimensional, locally compact, connected, locally connected metric space
conclusions: $L$ is a Lie group with finitely many connected components

nodes.name: Svarc-Milnor theorem (relating algebraic and geometric growth)
nodes.statement: Let $Y\to X$ be the universal covering and fix generators of $\Gamma=\pi_1(X)$. There is a constant $C_0>0$ such that for every $y\in Y$ and $r\ge 1$: $\mathrm{Vol}_y(C_0 r + C_0)\ge \#B(r)\ge \mathrm{Vol}_y(C_0^{-1} r)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Algebraic and geometric growth of fundamental group versus universal cover are mutually bounded by linear rescaling.

nodes.name: Polynomial growth equivalence (group vs. universal cover)
nodes.statement: $\pi_1(X)$ has polynomial growth iff the universal cover $Y$ of $X$ has polynomial volume growth.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial growth of fundamental group is equivalent to polynomial volume growth of the universal cover.

nodes.name: Polynomial growth of expanding manifolds (basic lemma)
nodes.statement: If $f:Y\to Y$ is a totally expanding smooth map with bounded Jacobian $\le C$ and uniformly expanding (i.e. $\mathrm{dist}(f(x),f(y))\ge (1+\varepsilon)\mathrm{dist}(x,y)$ for $\mathrm{dist}(x,y)\ge 1$, with $\varepsilon>0$), then $Y$ has polynomial growth.
nodes.statement_clean: Manifolds admitting bounded-Jacobian uniformly expanding maps have polynomial volume growth.

nodes.name: Proof of basic polynomial-growth lemma (LP396.1)
nodes.statement: Each ball $B$ of radius $r\ge 1$ is sent by $f$ onto a set containing a ball of radius $(1+\varepsilon)r$, with volume at most $C\cdot\mathrm{Vol}(B)$. Thus $\mathrm{Vol}_y((1+\varepsilon)r)\le C\,\mathrm{Vol}_y(r)$, which iterates to polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Splitting lemma
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ is a finitely generated subgroup of infinite index, then $\mathrm{growth}(\Gamma')\le \mathrm{growth}(\Gamma)-1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Infinite-index subgroups have growth degree at least one less than the ambient group.

nodes.name: Proof of splitting lemma (LP396.2)
nodes.statement: By the connectivity property of $X=\Gamma/\Gamma'$, every $r$-ball in $\Gamma$ contains at least $r+1$ elements $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r$ with distinct images in $X$. The translates $B'\alpha_i$ of $B'=B(r)\cap\Gamma'$ are disjoint and lie in $B(2r)$, giving $\#B(2r)\ge (r+1)\#B(r)\cap\Gamma'$.

nodes.name: Regularity lemma (existence of $i$-regular radii)
nodes.statement: There is a sequence $(r_i)$ tending to $\infty$ such that each $r_i$ is $i$-regular.
nodes.statement_clean: There exist arbitrarily large radii satisfying volume-doubling controls of arbitrary order.

nodes.name: Proof of regularity lemma (LP396.3)
nodes.statement: Start with $r_k=2^k$. Polynomial growth gives $\log b(2^k)\le C+kd\log 2$, yielding an infinite subsequence satisfying (a). The general inequality $b(2r)\le b(4r)/b(r)$ (proved via maximal $(2r+1)$-separated nets and connectivity), iterated, shows (a) implies (b) for large $r$.

nodes.name: Establish covering inequality $b(2r)\le b(4r)/b(r)$
nodes.statement: Take a maximal $(2r+1)$-separated set $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{N}$ in $B(3r)$; the $r$-balls about them are disjoint and the $2r$-balls cover $B(3r)$. Connectivity then gives the inequality $b(2r)/b(r)\le b(4r)/b(r)$.

nodes.name: Iterate to derive (b) from (a)
nodes.statement: Setting $f(r)=\log b(r)$, the inequality becomes $f(2r)\le 2f(r)-f(r/4)$. Iterating $j$ times for $r$ divisible by $16$ yields $f(2^j r)\le 16^j f(r)-(\ldots) f(r/4^j)$, which under (a) gives bound (b) with $\xi_j=16^{j+1}(d+1)$.

nodes.name: Algebraic lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group of polynomial growth and $L$ a Lie group with finitely many components. If for every finitely generated infinite subgroup $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ there is a finite-index subgroup $\Delta\subseteq\Gamma'$ admitting, for every $p$, a homomorphism $\Delta\to L$ with image of size $\ge p$, then $\Gamma$ is almost nilpotent.
nodes.statement_clean: If subgroups admit arbitrarily large representations into a Lie group, polynomial growth forces virtual nilpotence.
assumptions: $L$ Lie group with finitely many components
For each f.g. infinite $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ exists $\Delta\subset\Gamma'$ of finite index with arbitrarily large homomorphic images in $L$

nodes.name: Proof of algebraic lemma (LP396.4)
nodes.statement: Inductive proof using splitting lemma to assume f.g. infinite-index subgroups are almost nilpotent. Apply Jordan/Tits to obtain $\Delta'\subset\Delta$ of finite index whose commutator $[\Delta',\Delta']$ has infinite index. By lemma (b), $[\Delta',\Delta']$ is finitely generated, hence almost nilpotent, so $\Gamma$ is almost solvable and Milnor-Wolf gives almost nilpotent.

nodes.name: Inductive setup via splitting lemma
nodes.statement: By the splitting lemma, induct on growth: assume all finitely generated infinite-index subgroups are almost nilpotent.

nodes.name: Case split on image size of homomorphisms $\Delta\to L$
nodes.statement: Either all homomorphisms $\Delta\to L$ have finite image (apply Jordan via lemma (a)), or some has infinite image (apply Tits' theorem). In both cases obtain $\Delta'\subset\Delta$ with $[\Delta',\Delta']$ of infinite index.

nodes.name: Conclude via Milnor-Wolf
nodes.statement: By lemma (b), $[\Delta',\Delta']$ is finitely generated; the induction hypothesis makes it almost nilpotent. Hence $\Gamma$ is almost solvable, and Milnor-Wolf forces $\Gamma$ almost nilpotent.

nodes.name: Auxiliary lemma (a) on bounded-image homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let $L$ as above and $G$ finitely generated. If for every $p$ there is a homomorphism $G\to L$ with finite image of size $\ge p$, then $G$ has a finite-index subgroup $G'\subset G$ with $[G',G']\subset G'$ of infinite index, hence $G'$ admits a non-trivial homomorphism to $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Arbitrarily large finite quotients in L force a finite-index subgroup with infinite-index commutator.

nodes.name: Proof of auxiliary lemma (a)
nodes.statement: Take $G'$ to be the intersection of all subgroups of $G$ of index $\le q$ where $q$ is from Jordan's theorem; then $G'$ has the desired property.

nodes.name: Auxiliary lemma (b): commutator subgroup is finitely generated
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group of polynomial growth. Then the commutator subgroup $[\Gamma,\Gamma]$ is finitely generated.
nodes.statement_clean: Commutator subgroup of a polynomial-growth group is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Proof of lemma (b) (LP396.6)
nodes.statement: Reduce to: kernel $\Delta$ of any surjection $\Gamma\to\mathbb{Z}$ is f.g. Take generators $\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k$ with $g(\gamma_0)=z_0$, $\gamma_i\in\Delta$. Define $\Delta_m\subseteq\Delta$ generated by conjugates $\{\gamma_0^{-j}\gamma_i\gamma_0^j\}$ for $|j|\le m$. If $\Delta_m=\Delta_{m+1}$ for some $m$, done. Otherwise build $2^{m+1}$ distinct elements $\beta(\varepsilon_0,\ldots,\varepsilon_m)$ of norm $\le (k+1)(2m+1)$, contradicting polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Reduce to kernel of surjection to $\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the kernel $\Delta$ of any surjective homomorphism $g:\Gamma\to\mathbb{Z}$ is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Build chain $\Delta_m\subset\Delta$ via conjugation
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta_m$ be generated by $\{\gamma_0^{-j}\gamma_i\gamma_0^j : i\le k,\ |j|\le m\}$. The $\Delta_m$ are increasing with union $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Contradiction with polynomial growth
nodes.statement: If chain never stabilizes, exhibit $2^{m+1}$ products $\beta=\alpha_0^{\varepsilon_0}\cdots\alpha_m^{\varepsilon_m}$ of norm $\le (k+1)(2m+1)$, contradicting polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Corollary to algebraic lemma
nodes.statement: If each finitely generated infinite-index $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ has a finite-index subgroup $\Delta$ that is either Abelian or satisfies the hypotheses of the algebraic lemma, then $\Gamma$ is almost nilpotent.

nodes.name: Localization lemma
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be as in Montgomery-Zippin, $U\subset Y$ a non-empty open set, $p\in\mathbb{N}$. There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that any non-trivial isometry $\iota:Y\to Y$ with $\mathrm{dist}(u,\iota(u))<\varepsilon$ for $u\in U$ generates in the isometry group $L$ a subgroup of order at least $p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Small-displacement non-trivial isometries generate subgroups of arbitrarily large order in the isometry group.

nodes.name: Compactness criterion (Gromov-Hausdorff)
nodes.statement: Let $(X_j,x_j)$ be proper pointed metric spaces. If for each $r\ge 0$ the family $\{B_{x_j}(r)\}_j$ is uniformly compact, then a subsequence $(X_{j_k},x_{j_k})$ converges to a proper metric space $(Y,y)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Uniform compactness of metric balls implies subsequential pointed Gromov-Hausdorff convergence to a proper limit.
conclusions: A subsequence converges to a proper pointed metric space $(Y,y)$

nodes.name: Proof of compactness criterion (LP396.8)
nodes.statement: Reduce to the compact case via $r$-balls. Construct $\varepsilon_i$-nets via finite index sets $A_i$ and maps $I_j^i:A_i\to X_j$ that approximate. Embed each $X_j$ isometrically into a fixed compact space $F\subset F'$ (bounded function space on $A=\cup A_i$). Then apply compactness of compact subsets of $F$ under Hausdorff distance.

nodes.name: Construct $\varepsilon_i$-nets and approximating maps
nodes.statement: For $\varepsilon_i=2^{-i}$ and covering numbers $N_i$, define sequences $A_i$ and maps $I_j^i:A_i\to X_j$ such that the image is an $\varepsilon_i$-net, each refining the previous.

nodes.name: Embed into common compact space $F$
nodes.statement: Define $h_j(x)(a)=\mathrm{dist}(x, I_j(a))$, mapping each $X_j$ isometrically into the bounded function space $F'$; image lies in compact set $F$.

nodes.name: Extract convergent subsequence in $F$
nodes.statement: Compactness of compact subsets of $F$ under Hausdorff distance produces a subsequence converging to a compact $Y\subset F$, which gives $H(X_{j_k},Y)\to 0$.

nodes.name: Isometry lemma
nodes.statement: Let $(X_j,x_j)\Rightarrow(Y,y)$ with $Y$ proper, and $f_j:X_j\to X_j$ isometries with $\mathrm{dist}_j(x_j,f_j(x_j))\le C$. Then a subsequence $f_{j_k}$ converges to an isometry $Y\to Y$.
nodes.statement_clean: Isometries of converging metric spaces with bounded displacement subconverge to a limit isometry.

nodes.name: Homogeneity preserved under Gromov-Hausdorff convergence
nodes.statement: If each $X_j$ in a converging sequence is homogeneous (transitive isometry group), then the limit space $Y$ is also homogeneous.

nodes.name: Displacement lemma
nodes.statement: Suppose $D(\Gamma',r)$ is unbounded but for some $r_i\to\infty$, $r_i^{-1}D(\Gamma',r_i)\to 0$. Then for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a sequence $\alpha_i\in\Gamma$ with $\lim_i r_i^{-1}D(\alpha_i^{-1}\Gamma'\alpha_i, r_i)=\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conjugation can be tuned so the rescaled displacement converges to any prescribed value.

nodes.name: Proof of displacement lemma (LP396.10)
nodes.statement: Use connectivity to bound $D(\Gamma',r+m)\le D(\Gamma',r)+2m$ and conjugation bound $D(\alpha^{-1}\Gamma'\alpha,r)\le D(\Gamma',r)+2\|\alpha\|$. Choose $\alpha_i$ to interpolate displacement to $\varepsilon r_i$.

nodes.name: Main construction: limit isometry group is a Lie group
nodes.statement: For a group $\Gamma$ of polynomial growth with $i$-regular sequence $r_i\to\infty$, the rescaled spaces $(\Gamma_i,e_i)=(r_i^{-1}\Gamma,e)$ subconverge to a proper space $(Y,y)$ that is locally compact, connected, locally connected, finite-dimensional, with isometry group $L$ acting transitively. By Montgomery-Zippin, $L$ is a Lie group with finitely many components.
nodes.statement_clean: Rescaling polynomial-growth groups produces a metric limit whose isometry group is a Lie group.
conclusions: Limit space $Y$ is finite-dimensional, transitively isometric, Lie group $L=\mathrm{Isom}(Y)$ with finitely many components

nodes.name: Proof of main theorem (TP396.1)
nodes.statement: Apply algebraic lemma using main construction. For each f.g. $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$, build homomorphism $\Gamma'\to L$ via convergence of isometries; if image infinite, conditions of algebraic lemma are met. Otherwise either $\Gamma'$ is Abelian (when $D(\Gamma',r)$ bounded) or use displacement lemma plus localization lemma to find arbitrarily-large-image homomorphisms.

nodes.name: Build homomorphism $\Gamma'\to L$ via limit isometries
nodes.statement: Each $\gamma\in\Gamma'$ acts on $\Gamma_i$ by left translation; under convergence $(\Gamma_i,e_i)\to(Y,y)$, with bounded normalized translation $r_i^{-1}\|\gamma_i\|<\infty$, the sequence subconverges to an isometry $\iota_\gamma:Y\to Y$, giving a homomorphism $\Gamma'\to L$.

nodes.name: Case A: homomorphism has infinite image
nodes.statement: If $\gamma\mapsto\iota_\gamma$ has infinite image, the algebraic lemma applies with $L$ the Lie group from main construction; conclude $\Gamma$ almost nilpotent.

nodes.name: Case B: kernel of finite index, displacement bounded
nodes.statement: Pass to kernel $\Gamma''$ of finite index. If $D(\Gamma'',r)$ is bounded, $\Gamma''$ has finite-index Abelian subgroup; apply corollary to algebraic lemma.

nodes.name: Case C: unbounded displacement, apply displacement+localization
nodes.statement: Otherwise $D(\Gamma',r)$ unbounded but $r_i^{-1}D(\Gamma',r_i)\to 0$. Use displacement lemma to construct conjugating $\alpha_i$ giving small-displacement isometries on $Y$, then localization lemma yields arbitrarily-large-image homomorphisms; algebraic lemma concludes.

nodes.name: Effective version of main theorem
nodes.statement: For any positive integers $d,k$ there exist positive integers $R,N,q$ such that: if a group $\Gamma$ with fixed generators satisfies $\#B(r)\le r^d$ for $r=1,2,\ldots,R$, then $\Gamma$ contains a nilpotent subgroup of index $\le q$ and nilpotency degree $\le N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial growth on a finite range R already forces virtual nilpotence with bounded constants.

nodes.name: Geometric application (isometric action on Riemannian manifold)
nodes.statement: Let $V^n$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with Ricci $\ge -(n-1)K$, $K\ge 0$. Let $\Gamma$ be generated by isometries $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k$ of $V$. If for some $v\in V$, $\mathrm{dist}(v,\gamma(v))\ge \varepsilon>0$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma\setminus\{e\}$ and $\mathrm{dist}(v,\gamma_i(v))\le C\varepsilon$, then if $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small compared to $n,C,K$ (i.e. $\varepsilon<\mu_1(n,C,K)$), the group $\Gamma$ is almost nilpotent.
nodes.statement_clean: Discrete isometry groups with small-displacement generators on Ricci-bounded manifolds are virtually nilpotent.

nodes.name: Examples of manifolds of polynomial growth
nodes.statement: Examples include: (a) complete manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature; (b) real algebraic submanifolds in $\mathbb{R}^n$; (c) nilpotent Lie groups with left invariant metrics; (d) leaves of Anosov foliations.

nodes.name: Tangent cone construction via rescaling
nodes.statement: When $X$ has bounded local covering numbers, the rescaled spaces $(\lambda_j X, x)$ with $\lambda_j\to\infty$ subconverge to a proper space $(Y,y)$, the tangent cone of $X$ at $x$. For nilpotent Lie groups with left-invariant metric, $\lambda_j\to 0$ rescaling produces a non-Riemannian limit (Carnot metric).

nodes.name: Effective dependence of $R,N,q$ on $d,k$
nodes.statement: What is the dependence of the constants $R,N,q$ in the effective version on $d$ and $k$? In particular, does there exist an effective estimate of these numbers in terms of $d$ and $k$?

nodes.name: Classify expanding self-maps of compact manifolds
nodes.statement: Classify, up to topological conjugacy, expanding self-maps of compact manifolds; show they coincide with infra-nil-endomorphisms.

nodes.name: Bass-Wolf proposition: f-growth bound (Appendix)
nodes.statement: If $d_i$ denotes the rank of the abelian group $\Gamma_i/\Gamma_{i+1}$, then the nilpotent group $\Gamma$ has polynomial $f$-growth of degree $\le \sum i\,d_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Filtered nilpotent groups have polynomial f-growth degree bounded by sum i d_i.
conclusions: $\Gamma$ has polynomial $f$-growth of degree $\le \sum i d_i$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 (PrP396.1)
nodes.statement: Double induction on $a=\sup\{i:\Gamma_i\ne\{1\}\}$ and on minimum cardinality $m$ of generating sets of $\Gamma_a/\Gamma_{a+1}$. Choose generating set $E$ closed under commutators and inverses; for $y\in E_a$, build $\Gamma'$ generated by $E_a\setminus\{y\}$. Inductively show every word can be written as $y^s g'$ with $|s|\le r^a$ and $g'\in\Gamma'$ of bounded $f$-length, then count.

nodes.name: Setup double induction and choose generating set
nodes.statement: Induct on $a=\sup\{i:\Gamma_i\ne\{1\}\}$ and on $m=$ min generating cardinality of $\Gamma_a/\Gamma_{a+1}$. Choose $E$ with $|E_a|=m$, closed under commutators in $E\cup E^{-1}$, and minimal-exponent powers.

nodes.name: Reordering claim (*) by induction on $q$
nodes.statement: Inductively prove (*): every $E$-word can be reordered to start with the $\{y,y^{-1}\}$-letters, with $f$-length controlled by $n_i'\le n_i + (q-1) p_{i-a} + \binom{q-1}{2} p_{i-2a}+\cdots$.

nodes.name: Decomposition $g=y^s g'$ and counting
nodes.statement: Conclude (**): every $g\in\Gamma$ of $f$-length $\le (r,r^2,\ldots)$ can be written $g=y^s g'$ with $|s|\le r^a$ and $g'\in\Gamma'$ of $f$-length $\le (er-|s|, er^2-|s|,\ldots)$. Counting choices using induction hypothesis yields the polynomial bound.

nodes.name: Bass-Wolf two-sided polynomial growth bound
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be finitely generated nilpotent with descending central series of ranks $d_i$, and $d=\sum i d_i$. For any finite generating $E$ and $c(r)$ the count of elements of length $\le r$, there exist $c_1,c_2>0$ with $c_1 r^d \le c(r)\le c_2 r^d+1$. In particular, $\Gamma$ has polynomial growth of degree exactly $d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nilpotent groups have polynomial growth degree exactly sum i d_i (Bass-Wolf formula).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2 (PrP396.2)
nodes.statement: Upper bound is immediate from Proposition 1 applied to descending central series. Lower bound by induction on nilpotency class $e$: use Lemma 1 on the last term $Z$ of the descending central series to build many distinct elements of length $\le r/2$, combined with induction hypothesis on $\Gamma/Z$.

nodes.name: Tits Lemma 1: short word for $z^n$ in descending central series
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be finitely generated nilpotent of class $e$, $Z$ the last nontrivial term of its descending central series, $E$ a finite generating subset, and $z\in Z$. There exists $c>0$ such that, for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $z^n$ can be expressed as a word of length $\le c\,n^{1/e}$ in $E\cup E^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Powers of central elements admit short words of length growing like n^{1/e}.

nodes.name: Proof of Tits Lemma 1 (LP396.11)
nodes.statement: Induct on $e$; reduce to $z=[x,y]$. Choose smallest $n_1>n^{1/e}$, write $n=a_1 n_1^{e-1}+a_2$. Apply induction hypothesis to $\Gamma/Z$ and $y$ to find short representatives $y_1,y_2$ of length $\le c'n_1$. Then $z^n=[x,y_1]\cdot[x,y_2]\cdots$ has bounded length.

nodes.name: Tits Lemma 2 (special case of Milnor-Wolf)
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a group with a homomorphism $\sigma:L\to\mathbb{Z}$ whose kernel is finitely generated and almost nilpotent. Then $L$ is almost nilpotent or has exponential growth.
nodes.statement_clean: Z-extensions of f.g. almost-nilpotent kernels are almost nilpotent or exponential.

nodes.name: Tits Lemma 3: spectral lemma on automorphisms of free abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be free abelian and $\alpha:A\to A$ automorphism. (i) If $\alpha$ (extended to $A\otimes\mathbb{C}$) is semi-simple with all eigenvalues of absolute value 1, then $\alpha$ has finite order. (ii) If $\alpha$ has an eigenvalue of absolute value $\ge 2$, there exists $\lambda\in A$ such that the elements $\sum_{i=0}^\infty \varepsilon_i \alpha^i(\lambda)$ ($\varepsilon_i\in\{0,1\}$, finite support) are pairwise distinct.
nodes.statement_clean: Automorphisms of free abelian groups have finite order under unit eigenvalue conditions; large eigenvalues give exponential combinatorial richness.

nodes.name: Proof of Tits Lemma 3 (LP396.13)
nodes.statement: (i) Orbits of $\{\alpha^j\}$ in $A\otimes\mathbb{C}$ have compact closure, so orbits in $A$ are finite; (ii) Use linear form $\beta:A\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\beta\circ\alpha=p\beta$, $|p|\ge 2$; then $\beta(\sum\varepsilon_i\alpha^i\lambda)=\beta(\lambda)\sum\varepsilon_i p^i$ are pairwise distinct.

nodes.name: Proof of Tits Lemma 2 (LP396.12)
nodes.statement: Pick $z\in L$ with $\sigma(z)=1$, replace $L_1$ by max nilpotent normal subgroup. Take central series $(L_i)$ of $L_1$ normalized by $z$ with semi-simple $\alpha_i$ on infinite quotients. If all $\alpha_i$ have finite order, $z^s$ centralizes each $L_i/L_{i+1}$ for some $s$, so $\langle L_1, z^s\rangle$ is nilpotent of finite index. Otherwise apply Lemma 3(ii) to find $x\in L$ producing $2^N$ distinct elements; hence $L$ has exponential growth.

nodes.name: Geometric infinite-version of main theorem
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma$ has no torsion and each finitely generated subgroup $\Gamma'\subset\Gamma$ has growth at most $d$, then $\Gamma$ contains a nilpotent subgroup of finite index. Uses Auslander-Schenkman bound $\log\log q < 2d$ on the index $q$.

nodes.name: Volume rescaling inequality
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Vol}_y((1+\varepsilon)r)\le C\,\mathrm{Vol}_y(r)$ for all $r\ge 1$, where $y$ is the fixed point of $f$.

nodes.name: Covering inequality on group balls
nodes.statement: $b(2r)\le b(4r)/b(r)$, valid for all finitely generated groups.

nodes.name: Free Abelian group of rank 2
nodes.statement: For the free Abelian group of rank 2 with generators $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$, $\#B(r)=2N^2+2N+1$ for $r\in[N,N+1)$.

nodes.name: Free non-Abelian group of rank 2
nodes.statement: For the free non-Abelian group with two generators, $\#B(r)=2\cdot 3^N - 1$ for $r\in[N,N+1)$, exhibiting exponential growth.

nodes.name: Expanding map on torus $T^n$
nodes.statement: Each linear $\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ that sends $\mathbb{Z}^n$ into itself induces a map $T^n\to T^n$; this map is expanding iff all eigenvalues of the covering linear map have absolute value $>1$.

nodes.name: Tangent-cone limit of free Abelian group
nodes.statement: For the free Abelian group $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with the word metric of two generators, the rescaled sequence $(\lambda_i \Gamma, e)$ as $\lambda_i\to 0$ converges to $(\mathbb{R}^2, 0)$ with the Minkowski $\ell^1$ metric $\mathrm{dist}((a,b),(a',b'))=|a-a'|+|b-b'|$.
